case_title: Bharat Sher Singh Kalsia v. State of Bihar & Anr.
neutral_facts: The accused, a vendee, was involved in a dispute over the sale of land. The land-owners executed a Power of Attorney (PoA) granting authority to a PoA-holder to manage their property. The PoA-holder executed a sale deed in favor of the accused, and the accused paid the consideration amount. The land-owners sent a legal notice to the PoA-holder, demanding details of the sale, but received no response. The police registered a First Information Report (FIR) against the accused and the PoA-holder under various sections of the Indian Penal Code. The High Court rejected the prayer for quashing the FIR, but the Supreme Court ultimately quashed the FIR and the order taking cognizance, finding that the accused had no role in the execution of the PoA or any misdeed by the PoA-holder. A civil suit was filed by the land-owners against the PoA-holder, which was dismissed in favor of the accused, indicating that the PoA-holder was authorized to sell the property.
